//: The reference pipeline definition. This is checked in as a fixture, not as demo data:
PipelineGraphParserReferenceDefinitionTest loads *this file* and asserts what it parses to,
so a change to the stored format that nobody meant to make fails a test instead of surfacing
as a pipeline that no longer runs.
Every feature of the format that a stored definition can carry appears exactly once here:
version                - the format tag; absent means 1
options                - the documented per-node parameter object (split)
config                 - the legacy alias the editor used to write (work)
options + config       - both present; options wins (score)
affinity               - co-scheduling group (work, score)
source                 - the single entry node
blocking / syncToLoom  - the two per-node booleans, set away from their defaults
selective output ports - route.a / route.b, only one of which fires per item
a non-selective port   - route.label, which feeds a node that runs whichever branch fired
fan-out                - split.texts is MANY, so work and score run PER_ELEMENT
gather                 - gather's MANY inputs recombine the sequence, so it runs once
two edges, same pair   - split feeds work and gather-adjacent nodes on distinct ports
resultBatchSize        - pipeline-wide result batching
reuseResults           - reuse of previously computed node results
The node kinds are the synthetic ones from TestDescriptors, for the same reason the analyzer
tests use them: real kinds do not offer every port shape the format has to express, and
pinning the reference to whichever real node happens to fit today would break this fixture
every time that node is re-specified. The *format* is what is under test, not the catalogue.
